key_insight: VQE is vulnerable to multiple attack surfaces in cloud-style workflows, and a unified benchmark shows ZNE-manipulating noise attacks are the most damaging while parameter-level backdoors are comparatively weak.
engineering_relevance: For quantum software and hardware teams, this highlights the need to harden transpilation, mitigation, and service pipelines—not just the variational circuit itself—when deploying VQE-as-a-service.
method: Built VQE-AdvBench, a unified red-teaming benchmark for adversarial robustness of VQE.
Organized attacks by black-, gray-, and white-box access and evaluated seven representative scenarios.
Tested H2 and H3+ on five noise-calibrated IBM backends under a fixed molecule-ansatz-backend-metric setup.
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, noise-induced ZNE attacks caused up to 8.84× error amplification, QTrojan up to 7.52×, and QDoor only up to 1.37×.
watch_item: Results are benchmark- and setup-dependent, so severity may change with different molecules, ansätze, backends, or mitigation stacks.
paper_title: SoK: Adversarial Robustness of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver via Red-Teaming
